key_insight: A coupled pore-scale lattice Boltzmann model shows how temperature-driven salinity changes can reshape sea-ice brine channels non-uniformly through freezing.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables pore-scale analysis of coupled heat transfer, solute redistribution, and evolving geometry in phase-changing porous media.
method: Couple liquid solute transport with conjugate solid–liquid heat transfer.
Track direction-dependent interface motion using a link-based Volume-of-Pixel formulation.
Apply generalized Robin conditions for solute redistribution at moving interfaces.
evidence_signal: Thermal benchmarks validate phase change, literature tests show Robin-treatment convergence between first and second order, and diffusive brine-channel simulations recover ideal mushy-layer behaviour under appropriate scale separation.
watch_item: The sea-ice application is limited to a local, purely diffusive pore segment; performance with advective transport or larger-scale channel dynamics remains unestablished.
paper_title: A coupled lattice Boltzmann model for pore-scale mushy-layer dynamics with application to sea ice
